newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka unveils parts of draft constitution.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka unveils parts of draft constitution.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Wednesday released sections of a draft constitution which offered wide autonomy to minorities and was aimed at ending the country's ethnic war.

The new constitution, still being debated by a parliamentary select committee, would be proposed to the house within the next couple of months, Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told a news conference.
"This reflects the results of the work done by the select committee during the past 15 months," Peiris said.
He said last week's victory for the ruling People's Alliance at the local council elections strengthened the government's hand at taking the peace process forward.

Sri Lanka is in the process of introducing constitutional reforms to grant autonomy to minorities and end the war with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam rebels who demand an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east.
If approved by a two-thirds majority in parliament, the new constitution will be put to the people in a national referendum.
